items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: I didn't know Eastwood, but it's the harmonies that attracted Bix.

ctx.x: Were they very much in keeping with the impressionist schools or was it something parallel to that.

Let's see, I think that Eastwood Lane was a guy like Bix. There are several things in there that seem to me he got them from the effect of the Fawn, the orchestral effects. They both loved the orchestra, I'm sure. I didn't know Eastwood, but it's the harmonies that attracted Bix. He used to play -- he played a lot of his own harmony, the same type of thing. Only I think he developed them a little bit differently than Eastwood Lane. But are you familiar with the Land of the Loon.

No, that's what I said. There was just the name, which I have seen mentioned when musicians from that period we are talking about, their interests in the French impressionists, then Eastwood Lane's name would come up and I had never heard any of the things.

items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now, an American composer was always mentioned too, who I'm not familiar with, Eastwood Lane.
